reason: Both versions are carried by the IEX Order Book & Matching Engine project (50.9M messages, 1.2 µs p99, perf/core-pinning work), and no other bullet changed, so the decision rests only on the UMD Nano-Satellite role in B. Its Rust flight-software bullet gives some systems signal and backs up Rust in the skills list. But 'Cut communication latency 23% by building GraphQL interfaces' reads as a web-API latency claim with no baseline, which a low-latency engineer will discount, so it adds little for HFT. A keeps the page tighter and more focused on the C++/performance story.
risk_noted: B adds a fifth overlapping role during Fall 2026: the AWS Redmond internship (Sep-Dec 2026) plus four College Park 'Present' roles (Amazon Leo contract, UMIACS, Nano-Satellite, TerpLabs). A skeptic will doubt how much was done in each. The 23% GraphQL latency number is vague (latency of what, measured how?) and could invite awkward interview questions. 'Systems Engineer' on a student team may read as an inflated title.
